EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Date of service: 10/28/2023, arrival 07:50

CC: short of breath, ankles swollen.

HPI: 71M with systemic AL amyloidosis with cardiac involvement (treatment completed March), chronic HFrEF, CAD s/p LAD stent, CKD 3b, polymyositis on prednisone and azathioprine, HTN, T2DM. Two days of increasing breathlessness and swelling of both ankles. Earlier this week had an episode of severe chest pain that went away by itself; none since.

Meds: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, metformin 1000 BID, furosemide 40, aspirin 81, prednisone 5, azathioprine 100, acetaminophen PRN.
Allergies: hydrochlorothiazide (angioedema, electrolyte abnormalities).

Exam: BP 90/60, HR 110, RR 22, SpO2 92% on room air. JVD. Crackles at both bases. 2+ pitting edema of both ankles. Abdomen soft, nontender.

Data: AST 2,500, ALT 2,300, total bilirubin 1.2, alkaline phosphatase 100, INR 1.1. hs-troponin T 64, repeat 67 ng/L at 3 hours. ECG: sinus tachycardia with ST depression in the anterior leads.

MDM: Hypotension with congestion in a patient with amyloid cardiomyopathy. Transaminases in the thousands with near-normal bilirubin and INR - pattern of ischemic (hypoperfusion) liver injury. Troponin elevated but flat, consistent with chronic myocardial injury from amyloid rather than an acute coronary syndrome; cardiology consulted in the ED and agrees. Antihypertensives held.

Disposition: admitted to cardiology.

reports.text:
TRANSTHORACIC ECHOCARDIOGRAM
Indication: hypotension, heart failure, known cardiac amyloidosis.
Left ventricle: increased wall thickness. Normal cavity size. LVEF 35%. No new regional wall motion abnormality compared with prior study.
Right ventricle: normal size.
Valves: no significant valvular disease.
Pericardium: no effusion.
reports.conclusion: Increased left ventricular wall thickness, LVEF 35%, no new regional wall motion abnormality.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY - CARDIOLOGY
Admitted: 10/28/2023   Discharged: 11/03/2023

Principal problem: hypotension with congestion in amyloid cardiomyopathy (chronic HFrEF).
Secondary: hepatic dysfunction - ischemic hepatitis from low blood pressure.

Course: Admitted from the ED with BP 90/60, HR 110, SpO2 92%, JVD, basilar crackles and ankle edema; AST 2,500 and ALT 2,300 with bilirubin 1.2 and INR 1.1; anterior ST depressions; hs-troponin T 64 then 67 (flat). Lisinopril and amlodipine held; metformin and azathioprine held for the liver injury. Blood pressure recovered over the first 24 hours, after which he was diuresed with IV furosemide. Echo 10/29: increased wall thickness, LVEF 35%, no new regional wall motion abnormality. No chest pain during the stay. Transaminases fell daily; AST 180 and ALT 610 on the day of discharge. Prednisone 5 mg continued.

Discharge medications:
- furosemide 40 mg every morning
- aspirin 81 mg daily
- prednisone 5 mg daily
- acetaminophen as needed (no more than 2 g/day until liver tests normalize)
HELD until primary care follow-up: lisinopril 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg.
HELD until liver tests normalize: metformin 1000 mg BID, azathioprine 100 mg (rheumatology informed).
Allergies: hydrochlorothiazide (angioedema, electrolyte abnormalities).

Follow-up: primary care within 1 week with liver tests and BMP; cardiology in 4-6 weeks.

1. Ischemic hepatitis - resolving. Recheck liver tests in 4 weeks; metformin and azathioprine stay on hold until normal.

Medication reconciliation completed.

History: 72-year-old man with systemic AL amyloidosis with cardiac involvement, chronic HFrEF, CAD s/p LAD stent, CKD 3b, polymyositis, hypertension and type 2 diabetes; prior history of hepatic dysfunction (2023).
